mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate (as measured by the current value relative to the prior 3-month average) compresses discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.0% (as measured by the current value) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous expansion in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where both HOUST > 1300 and RSAFS > 500000, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), the Federal Reserve is likely to implement monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) relative to the prior 3-month average indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS has increased over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 105.0 (as measured by the current value) signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate profits and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO falls below 105.0, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When both unemployment rate (UNRATE) and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) are trending downward, it indicates a policy response to economic softening, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where both UNRATE and FEDFUNDS are declining, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In tight labor market regimes (UNRATE < 4.0%), wage pressures build and inflation expectations rise, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which reduces equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE is below 4.0%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
